subject: Information Theory
title: Rate-Distortion Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Rate-Distortion Theory.

hook.text: How much can you compress a photo before it looks bad? Shannon proved there's a precise tradeoff curve.

buildup.text: Rate-distortion theory: for any acceptable distortion level, there's a minimum bit rate—and vice versa.

discovery.text: Shannon's rate-distortion function R(D) maps each distortion D to the minimum bits per symbol needed.

twist.text: You can't compress below R(D) without exceeding distortion D. It's a fundamental limit, like channel capacity.

climax.text: Modern codecs like H.265 and AV1 are engineered to ride as close to this curve as possible.

punchline.text: Less bits means more distortion. Shannon drew the curve.

quiz.question: What does rate-distortion theory describe?
options: The tradeoff between compression rate and acceptable distortion
